headline: Energy Transition Leader | Board Advisor | EY Global Coordinating Partner | EY Americas Energy & Resources Power & Utilities
about:
The energy sector is transforming significantly, shaped by decarbonization, renewable
integration, and digitalization. I advise clients on navigating these complexities with a focus on
advancing the energy transition, modernizing grid and water infrastructure, and embedding
digital technologies. My work centers on building resilient, future-ready organizations that deliver
sustainable growth and long-term value in an evolving market.

As an EY Global Coordinating Partner, and former Americas Energy & Resources Industry Leader, I advise boards and executive teams on operational improvements, digital transformation strategies, and
navigating the risks and trade-offs associated with emerging technologies, including AI,
e-mobility, and smart grid innovation. I have more than 30 years of leadership experience across
Power and Utilities, Water and Wastewater, Oil and Gas, and Chemicals.

Previously, I also served as EY’s Americas Power and Utilities Sector Leader and Lead Client
Partner for three of the firm's largest energy clients, guiding enterprise-wide innovation and
transformation initiatives to support their journeys toward net-zero emissions. Over the course of
my career, I have led global teams across the United States, Latin America, Canada, India, and
the Philippines, delivering successful strategic outcomes in both mature and emerging markets.

In addition to my client work, I am committed to advancing diversity and inclusion across the
energy sector. I actively support the development of women executives through EY’s Women in
Energy Network and the Women’s Energy Network, and I lead the Power Energy Network, an
initiative focused on growing minority-owned businesses serving the energy industry.

I believe that strong leadership, diverse perspectives, and continuous innovation are essential to
building a clean energy future, and I am dedicated to helping shape that future across both
energy and water ecosystems.

honorsAndAwards.title: INROADS Rising Star Award
honorsAndAwards.description:
In 1970, Frank C. Carr, INROADS’ late founder, planted the seeds for what INROADS has become today. Inspired by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s landmark “I Have a Dream” speech, Frank quit his executive-level corporate day job in Chicago, IL and made a commitment to taking swift and decisive action to increase ethnically diverse employees in corporate management in the US, and to help change the way these candidates gained entry into the business world.
 The INROADS mission is to develop and place talented underserved youth in business and in industry, and prepare them for corporate and community leadership. From its founding in 1970 by business executive Frank C. Carr, ( MLK 1995 Salute to Greatness Recipient) INROADS has grown into a nationally recognized 501 © (3) nonprofit, impacting the lives of over 154,000 underrepresented youth, with over 50% being girls of color. 
The Rising Star Award recognizes individuals who has demonstrated exceptional leadership as well as embody and honor the INROADS mission. I was awarded based off my involved in the community with Junior Achievement, my continued support through leadership at EY and contribution with INROADS through mentoring students at Kennesaw State University all while serving as INROADS Alumni Association Vice President. My involvement in Securing funds and conducting the INROADS Alumni Association and EY Leadership Panel (The Art of Inclusion: Building a Diverse Team for a Diverse World) in March 2018, aligns with the mission of INROADS.
 The Benefit Gala’s goal serves as INROADS’ signature, most high-profile event. This charitable affair recognizes the achievements of our students, community/philanthropic leadership and honors corporate responsibility. As an honoree, I joined previous recipients, some of which have included ¬¬¬-Will & Jada Smith Family Foundation, XEOX’s former CEO Ursula Burns, PWC’s CEO Tim Ryan and General & Mrs. Colin Powell.

about:
Change Management | Consulting | PMO Leadership | Program Management Consulting | Strategy Development and Execution 

I love exploring new possibilities and challenging the status quo with novel ways of doing business that position organizations for organizational change and transformation.  

My curious nature drives me to collaborate with others to find solutions and to achieve goals even in the face of insurmountable challenges. 

As a thought leader and C-Suite consultant for the last decade, I have demonstrated strong executive influence and strategic agility. I excel in ambiguous, complex situations. My ability to create a strategy, develop a plan to execute, and inspire people to bring it to life is rare. I bring a commitment to the big picture coupled with the expertise to develop a path to reach the goal.

Throughout my career, I have motivated and guided organizations through change. Some examples include:

•	Defining a strategy for a 41-location, fast-growing business that informed R&D innovation and decisions, and enabled a 32% to 27% cost reduction. 
•	Positioning a company to grow 412% in less than 8 years by transforming the organization from ad hoc operations to standard repeatable processes over a 12-month period.
•	Leading an organizational change management (OCM) initiative that impacted more than 3,600 operational leaders, enabling them to improve cost margins by 50 basis points.

As a leader, I build relationships, trust, and confidence with my teams, which empowers them to achieve high levels of performance. I empower them to deliver results, while cultivating a fun and collaborative work environment where we share our knowledge and experiences. I thrive on developing people and helping them grow through teaching, mentoring, and coaching.

Outside of work, I spend my time volunteering in my local community, sharing good food with even better friends, cycling, and reading.

headline: Cybersecurity, AI Governance, Risk, Compliance, & Legal Thought Leader | EY | Ex-DocuSign | Financial Services | Healthcare | Technology
topSkills: Artificial Intelligence (AI) • Cybersecurity • Cyberlaw • Data Governance • Product Development
about:
I bridge the critical gap between executive leadership, cybersecurity, and the law.

With over 15 years of leadership, I have built my career on a unique foundation: the hands-on, technical experience of a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) combined with the strategic, internal perspective of an in-house attorney for global SaaS and technology companies.

I partner with C-suite executives and boards to translate complex global regulations (like GDPR, NIS2, DORA) and emerging risks (like AI Governance) into actionable, business-driven strategy. My expertise is not just theoretical or academic; I have built enterprise security and trust programs from the ground up, engineered security-by-design into product lifecycles (SDLC), and provided hands-on legal counsel during incident response.

My passion is helping organizations navigate their most complex challenges. Whether it is architecting a security program to meet CMMC, CCPA, or NYDFS Part 500 standards, preparing a client for a third-party audit, or advising on the risks and opportunities of Generative AI, I provide clear, pragmatic guidance that protects the business and enables growth.

Core Competencies:

► AI Governance & Risk Management (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act)
► Enterprise Cybersecurity Strategy & Program Development
► Global Privacy & Data Protection (GDPR, CCPA, NIS2, DORA)
► CISO & Legal Counsel Advisory to Boards & C-Suite
► Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)
► Incident Response & Crisis Management
► Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM)
► Regulatory Audits & Compliance (HITRUST, ISO 27001, CMMC, NYDFS Part 500, CCPA)

My hybrid expertise includes key certifications across both domains: ISC2 CISSP & CCSP for technical security, and IAPP CIPP/E, CIPP/US, & AIGP for privacy and AI governance.

publications.title: How can the intelligent age propel private markets
Agentic AI: Navigating the Uncharted Waters of Non-Human Identity and Liability
publications.description: Agentic AI empowers automation and decision-making, but also expands the attack surface, raising novel legal and security challenges.  We will delve into the risks of compromised agents, identity attacks, tool misuse, and goal manipulation, examining potential liabilities under existing legal frameworks in the absence of specific AI agent regulations.  We will also analyze the OWASP TOP for LLM Applications and GenAI Data Security Best Practices, including Excessive Agency and Functionality, as well as gaps in existing threat-modeling frameworks for addressing the agentic AI attack surface, particularly when multiple AI agents interact within an ecosystem.

publications.title: Vendor Contract Reviews: Managing Privacy, Cybersecurity and AI Risks
publications.description: As organizations increasingly rely on third-party vendors, the downstream use of data - particularly in AI applications - has become a critical area for privacy, cybersecurity and compliance professionals.  Through practical contract analysis sessions, tabletop exercises and case studies, this one-day workshop provides a comprehensive guide to reviewing vendor contracts to address legal, operational and ethical risk while aligning with global regulations.

DeepSeek, Personal Data Privacy and National Security
publications.description: In the short time since Chinese AI developer DeekSeek released its R1 open-source large language model (LLM) into the marketplace, a firestorm of controversy has developed that touches multiple aspects of its use, including U.S. national security. In addition to a complete ban on its use within Italy, several national governments and U.S. states have banned its use on employee devices. Is R1 truly a threat, and if so, how? More importantly, what are the legal implications and requirements of its use? In this fireside chat, a team of AI, cybersecurity, and privacy attorneys join Brandon Dunlap to discuss the many legal aspects of using R1 and other open-source LLMs.

publications.title: Do CISOs Need Their Own Legal Counsel? Some Lessons from SolarWinds and Uber
publications.description: In October 2023, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filed a civil complaint against SolarWinds and its CISO, Timothy Brown. The charges stemmed from the September 2019 intrusion by threat actors into SolarWinds, which affected some 18,000 customers. This action by the SEC is likely the first time the agency targeted a CISO for alleged cybersecurity failures. It comes on the heels of the October 2022 criminal conviction of Uber CSO Joe Sullivan for withholding information about a 2016 breach at Uber from federal investigators. All of this raises an important issue for CISOs: Should they have their own legal counsel to guide them on legal compliance and working with regulatory agencies? And if so, who should pay – them, or their employers? In this presentation by cybersecurity attorneys, we’ll take a deep dive into the hard choices that modern CISOs face and some possible ways forward.

Some Legal Perspectives on the Crowdstrike Outage
publications.description: In July 2024 a routine configuration update made by anti-malware vendor CrowdStrike to its Falcon Sensor platform contained a bug that caused catastrophic failures to the Windows machines running it, resulting in worldwide outages at airlines, banks, and hospitals. Preliminary estimates of damages exceeding $5 billion have been publicized, with that figure likely to go much higher. This outage raises some important legal questions, perhaps the most important of which is: Who’s liable? The answers may surprise you. In this session, a panel of cybersecurity attorneys will conduct a deep dive into this event and explain who is (and isn’t) liable and for how much. They will also explain how liability for software functions in the U.S. as well as globally, and what InfoSec professionals should know when negotiating software licensing agreements.

publications.title: Considerations for Conducting Artificial Intelligence Impact Assessments

Legal Perspectives on the NIST AI Risk Management Framework
publications.description: The January 26, 2023, release of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) came at a particularly auspicious time: ChatGPT had been released just a month earlier and quickly demonstrated the ability to identify weaknesses in code, generate malware and craft convincing phishing emails. NIST’s rationale for the development of the framework was to better manage risks associated with AI for individuals, organizations and society associated. In this session, data protection attorneys will offer their perspectives on the potential for the framework to manage risks for your organization.

publications.title: What ChatGPT Means for Your InfoSec Program
publications.description: Since its inception, ChatGPT has sent shockwaves through the cybersecurity and privacy communities with its abilities to identify weaknesses in code, generate malware and craft convincing phishing emails. Moreover, as ChatGPT and other AI software grow in sophistication, their potential for harm will grow as well. In this session, data protection attorneys will offer their perspectives and considerations for your InfoSec program

publications.description: Employee monitoring and insider risk remain a critical area of concern for organizations big and small.  An effective program must balance requirements to protect consumer and corporate information and privacy, vs the privacy of employees and the culture of the company.  The session will describe how companies can tackle the insider risk issues and build a program that balances the relevant interests.  The panelists will describe both operational steps to effectuate an insider program and also the legal questions to address in developing the program, both in the United States and globally.  Participants will learn about the threat landscape and trends, how to engage with partners in the company to build out the program, and legal issues around employee monitoring.

about:
Antoine Mindjimba is a Partner at EY, where he leads the Culture Evolution and Diversity & Inclusion service offerings in Canada. He has over 18 years of consulting experience, specializing in change management, culture transformation, training, and behavioral economics. He holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and a Black Leaders Program certificate from Stanford University Graduate School of Business.

Antoine leverages his unique background as a former professional international ice hockey player and a member of the French National and Olympic Teams to motivate and develop high-potential individuals and teams. He has deep experience in the global rollout of change management and training programs across various industries, and has developed change management KPIs and dashboards to track the effectiveness of change initiatives. He is passionate about creating inclusive and high-performing cultures that drive business results and social impact.

publications.title: Governing the Cloud
publications.description:
Once an emerging technology, cloud computing services have arrived, and they are here to stay.

Cloud allows for increased business agility, faster speed to market, lower information technology costs and happier customers.

According to our survey, cloud adoption increased nearly 100% from 2010 to 2012. Yet, within many organizations, IT has been reluctant to embrace cloud as a viable solution.

Undeterred, business units are often going it alone, procuring cloud services without IT’s involvement. The result is a shadow IT environment that is tough to manage, difficult to operate and nearly impossible to secure.

Organizations seeking to take advantage of cloud computing to create a more nimble, digitally integrated business environment are quickly learning that cloud services need to be adopted as an integral part of the organization’s existing operating model. However, this can create unforeseen risks if businesses do not simultaneously develop a cloud governance model to establish standards for the business to follow and create clear direction and consistency in managing cloud services.

As a Communication and Media capstone project, I reviewed grey literature and conducted a structured (quantitative) and unstructured (qualitative) analysis, and data visualization work on original data pertaining to university-industry relations activities in the Chicago metro area.

My analysis addressed the ways in which R&D-intensive universities (which extensively produce cutting-edge inventions, like advanced digital innovations) contribute to their local economies and communities, and the roles of bridge-unites and professionals facilitating it.

The project directly aided and informed the PI, Dr. Muzammil Hussain, on policy advisory research engagements for the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) in December 2019.

Shikhar is also a startup mentor and associated with multiple incubation centres. He is a thought leader in the market and publishes points of view across energy and mobility-related themes. He built and managed large teams in India focused on sales enablement, client engagements, demand generation, business insights, and data analytics. publications.title: Nature-Based Solutions in ASEAN: From Compliance Burden to Strategic Asset
publications.description: As investment in NbS gains traction across Southeast Asia—from mangrove restoration to regenerative agriculture—corporates are rethinking how sustainability can contribute to long-term enterprise value. This article explores how Japanese companies can engage in credible, locally grounded NbS projects that deliver not only climate impact, but also measurable financial returns and reputational value. The key is integration: aligning carbon strategies with core business objectives and regional realities.

publications.title: ASEAN's Rapid Sustainability Shift: Strategic Imperatives and Growth Paths for Japanese Companies
publications.description:
Developed a strategic insight piece on emerging sustainability trend

Sustainability policies in ASEAN are having a significant impact on corporate management, demanding strategic responses from businesses. Carbon pricing initiatives, particularly in Singapore, are gaining momentum, while carbon credit markets leveraging Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are attracting increasing attention as promising investment opportunities. Japanese companies must adapt to these structural changes and strategically capture new growth opportunities.
